chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the testimony of a child of fornication – is it permissible? He said: No. I said: Al-Hakam ibn 'Atiyyah claims that it is permissible, so he (peace be upon him) said: O Allah, do not forgive his sin! Allah was not addressing Al-Hakam when He said: 'It is a reminder for you and your people.' Let Al-Hakam go to the right and to the left, for by Allah, he will not find knowledge except with the People of the House upon whom Jibril (peace be upon him) descended.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.وَلَدِ الزِّنَا: Child born out of wedlock (child of fornication)

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child of fornication accepted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rejects the testimony of the Walad Zina, specifically refuting Al-Hakam ibn 'Atiyyah by citing Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:44 to argue that the Quranic revelation was a specific reminder for the Prophet and his people, not a general source of independent jurisprudential authority for him. This highlights the Shia principle of 'Ilm (knowledge) being preserved primarily within the Ahl al-Bayt, who received the divine inspiration of Jibril, thereby distinguishing their infallible understanding from other scholars.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/147] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Masud from Ali b. al-Hasan b. Fadhal from al-Abbas b. A`mir and Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Hukaym from Aban b. Uthman from Abi Basir who said:

I asked Aba Ja’far عليه السلام about the Shahada (giving witness) of a Walad Zina (child born out of Nikah) – is it permissible? he عليه السلام said: No. I said: al-Hakam b. Utayba holds it to be permissible, so he عليه السلام said: O Allah – do not forgive his sin! Allah was not addressing al-Hakam when He said: ‘it is a reminder unto you and your Qawm (relations)’ [43:44]. al-Hakam can go to the right and to the left, for by Allah he will not find true knowledge except with the Ahl al-Bayt upon whom Jibril عليه السلام descended.
